claims.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
claims.evidence: For every graph, C is a vertex cover iff its complement is independent, so τ(G)=n−α(G). Hence τ(G)≤k iff G has an independent (n−k)-set, which under graph complementation is equivalent to containing K_{n−k}; this proves F=2^N−T. For k=1, every nonempty admissible graph is a nonempty subgraph of a star; one-edge graphs have exactly two possible centers and graphs with at least two edges have one, giving the stated correction. The remaining endpoint formulas follow from independent sets of sizes n, 2, 1, and 0. Exhaustive enumeration confirmed every applicable identity for 0≤n≤6.
claims.search_method: Independent combinatorial proof followed by exact-integer enumeration of all labelled graphs through n=6.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
claims.evidence: For each k-set C there are exactly q possible edges incident with C and therefore 2^q generated graphs. Every graph with τ≤k has a k-cover by extending a smaller cover, and retaining it only for the first k-cover in a fixed order counts it exactly once. Testing all k-sets for each generated pair gives poly(n)·binom(n,k)^2·2^q=2^{q+O(n)} time. Iterators, one graph mask, and the O(n²)-bit answer counter use polynomial space. Since q≤nk, k=o(n) makes the exponent o(n²); k=O(n/log n) is such a regime. Exact enumeration verified the generator, pair count, uniqueness, and final answer for every 0≤k≤n≤6.
claims.search_method: Algorithm-invariant and complexity proof, plus exhaustive exact canonical-generator checks for n≤6.

claims.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
claims.evidence: Fix a t-cover C and let I be its independent complement. For nonempty H-independent X⊆C, writing U_X=N_I(X), the cover (C\X)∪U_X proves that C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every X. Under that condition, every alternative minimum cover is exactly of this form with equality. Comparing equal-sized subsets lexicographically shows that C is first exactly when min X<min U_X in every equality case. Counts capped at |X|+1 and one low-label bit therefore retain precisely the needed information. There are at most 2^t−1 coordinates and at most 2(t+2) values per coordinate; enumerating H and the 2^t neighborhood types yields the displayed fixed-parameter bound. The implemented DP and both cover predicates matched brute force for every n≤6 and every t.
claims.search_method: Structural derivation of the minimum/lex-first predicates, state-space analysis, and exact DP-versus-brute-force comparison.

claims.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
claims.evidence: Let X(G) count independent m-sets. Summing over the chosen set gives Σ_G X(G)=S1. For an ordered pair of m-sets meeting in j vertices, exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) distinct edges are forbidden, giving the stated S2=Σ_G X(G)^2 with no missing symmetry factor. Then 1_{X>0}≤X gives the upper bound, Cauchy–Schwarz gives F≥ceil(S1²/S2), and fixing one independent m-set gives F≥2^q. Finally S1≤2^{q+n}. Exact enumeration verified both moment identities and every integer bound for all 1≤m≤n≤6.
claims.search_method: Independent ordered-pair moment derivation and exhaustive exact-integer checking through n=6.

claims.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
claims.evidence: P_n counts a bipartite graph together with a labelled proper two-coloring, so a graph with c connected components has weight 2^c. The convolution counts the same weight by assigning every component wholly to one of two labelled vertex blocks and choosing the induced bipartite graph on each block. Its endpoint terms are both B_n, proving the recurrence. It uses polynomially many operations on O(n²)-bit integers. Since every bipartite graph is triangle-free, T(n,3)≥B_n and subtraction reverses this to the stated upper bound. Direct counts through n=6 were 1,1,2,7,41,376,5177 and matched the recurrence, which was also evaluated exactly through n=12.
claims.search_method: Independent weighted double-counting proof, exhaustive bipartiteness testing through n=6, and exact recurrence evaluation through n=12.

target_evidence: The exact target requests one exact 2^{o(n²)} algorithm for arbitrary input n,k. The draft does not establish that uniform result: for k=n/2 its general algorithm has q=(3n²−2n)/8=Θ(n²); the second algorithm is polynomial only for fixed k; and at k=n−3 the draft supplies a reduction to exact triangle-free-graph enumeration and computable bounds, not the requested exact subquadratic-exponent count. Nevertheless, the exact algorithm for every regime k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n), is correct and material partial progress. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, and its final writeup explicitly says the full uniform target remains unresolved, so that resolution claim is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
